citation.title: Process-aware topology optimization leveraging deep learning surrogate model-based functions for laser powder bed fusion
citation.authors: Praveen S. Vulimiri; Shane Garner; Albert C. To
citation.version_coded: abstract only (reconstructed from OpenAlex, https://api.openalex.org/works/W7125482830); no legal full-text route could be reached

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The abstract states that a deep-learning surrogate, trained on elastoplastic finite-element (inherent-strain) simulations of stainless steel 316L, is used inside a topology optimization that minimizes LPBF build distortion, with the surrogate evaluated about 100 times faster than the traditional (classical) simulation it replaces, while yielding comparable mechanical performance and no build failures.
claim.key_phrase: surrogate model evaluation approximately 100 times faster than traditional simulation
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Stated directly in the abstract ('approximately 100 times faster than traditional simulation'); not independently verified against the full text, and it is unclear from the abstract alone whether this is a per-evaluation surrogate-vs-FEA figure or a full optimization-loop figure.
claim.alternatives: None identifiable from the abstract alone; the abstract also separately notes the optimized designs have 'reduced distortion' and 'comparable mechanical performance without build failures' relative to a conventional design, which is a design-quality comparison but is not given a number.

The screening decision is kept as include (I-SPEED, since the abstract gives an explicit, numeric speed comparison against 'traditional simulation') per the access rules. included.stratum is set to 'none' rather than 'speed', per the record validator (audit.coding.validate_records), which treats stratum as undetermined for any record that is not read in full text; the abstract-level content still points to a speed-type primary outcome (see claim fields). method_family is coded 'surrogate_mlp_gp' (a deep-learning surrogate trained on FEA data, used for fast sensitivity/response evaluation inside the optimization loop, per the abstract); physics is coded 'other' because the objective (LPBF-process-induced surface distortion and per-layer vertical displacement, via an inherent-strain elastoplastic model) does not cleanly match compliance, stress, thermal, compliant_mechanism, multiphysics or metamaterial_homogenization; dim is coded '3d' (LPBF-manufactured parts, 'hundreds of thousands of design variables', physically printed and tested).
